planting.note: Direct sow in fall to allow winter cold stratification, or plant divisions in spring in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Black Snakeroot is a native woodland member of the carrot family with distinctive round, bristly seed heads.

directions: Plant in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, similar to the woodland conditions where it grows wild across eastern and central North America. Black Snakeroot bears small, greenish-white flower clusters in late spring on branching stems above deeply divided, palmate leaves, followed by distinctive round, bur-like seed heads covered in hooked bristles that catch on fur and clothing to disperse. Despite the common name it has no confirmed effect on snakebite; the name reflects historical folk use rather than proven medicinal value. It self-sows readily in a woodland garden and provides early-season nectar for small native bees and flies before many showier woodland wildflowers bloom.

planting.note: Plant nursery-propagated divisions in spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in full to partial shade; Pyrola species are notoriously difficult to transplant successfully because of a dependence on specific soil mycorrhizal fungi, so purchase only nursery-grown stock and disturb roots as little as possible.

directions: Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich woodland soil in full to partial shade, and avoid disturbing the roots more than necessary, since this species relies on a close relationship with soil fungi that makes it slow to establish after transplanting. Elliptic Shinleaf forms a low evergreen rosette of glossy, elliptical leaves from which a slender flowering stalk rises in summer, bearing a loose spike of nodding, waxy, greenish-white flowers with a sweet fragrance and a distinctive curved style. It spreads slowly by rhizomes in the deep leaf litter of rich, undisturbed forest floors, making it best suited to an established woodland garden rather than a young or heavily amended bed. Leave fallen leaves in place as mulch to maintain the organic, fungus-rich soil layer it depends on.
